articles.title_orig: Amelia Earhart expedition team heads to island of huge, hunting crabs
articles.title_zh: Amelia Earhart expedition team heads to island of huge, hunting crabs
articles.content_orig:
A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the plane wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart.
The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance.
The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate.
The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.
Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938.
The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.
They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country.
When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll's reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.
"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said.
Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her Electra twin-engine plane when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937.
From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California.
But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel.
Earhart's disappearance spawned numerous theories - from a simple crash due to fuel exhaustion to more elaborate claims of interference.
The official explanation is that the plane suffered communication problems while the two struggled to find the island, and Earhart eventually crashed into the ocean when she ran out of fuel.
While this version of events is largely accepted, no physical evidence has ever been recovered.
One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.
Images of the so-called Taraia Object show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters.
But some - including rival explorers - have expressed scepticism that this could be a plane, let alone Earhart's.
Ric Gillespie, who specialises in recovering historic aircraft wrecks, told news agency Reuters that the object looked like a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the nearby water.
"I'd love to find that airplane. It ain't gonna happen," he said.
The researchers en route to the island credit Gillespie with previously finding evidence of a human presence on the atoll in the 1930s and forensic analysis of skeletal remains found there in the 1940s they say lend credence to their theory.
But Gillespie suspects Earhart's plane had likely broken apart and its fragments carried into the depths of the Pacific long ago.
Previous attempts to find her Electra have also come up short.
In 2024, a group of researchers said they may have found it lying around 4,877m (16,000ft) below the surface near Howland Island through sonar imaging - but this was later confirmed to be a rock formation.
Similarly, an expedition in 2019, conducted by the marine archaeologist who discovered the Titanic wreck, to investigate a photograph of what might have been a landing gear protruding from the water near Nikumaroro also failed to find anything.

articles.title_orig: Pope at Angelus: Christian joy is ‘gift of God for world’s salvation’
articles.title_zh: Pope at Angelus: Christian joy is ‘gift of God for world’s salvation’
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV prayed the noon-day Marian prayer of the Angelus on Sunday with pilgrims gathered in St. Peterâs Square.
As the Church celebrated the Twenty-Eighth Sunday in Ordinary Time, the Gospel reading recounted Jesusâ parable of a wedding feast prepared by a king for his son.
In his address, the Pope recalled St. Thomas Aquinasâ saying that âgoodness, by its very nature, tends to spread (â Bonum dicitur diffusivum sui â).â
Read the full text of the Pope's Angelus address
Like the king in the story, we too desire to spread our happiness with others.
However, noted the Pope, Jesusâ parable points out the lack of welcome the kingâs joy received.
âSome are annoyed, insult the kingâs messengers and even kill them,â he said. âUnfortunately, this can happen to us, too, for the good we offer to do is not always understood, recognized or appreciated.â
Yet, he added, we must not be discouraged when we face rejection but rather go ahead with our plans and invite others to share our joy, like the king.
Pope Leo then explored the question of whom the main characters in the story represent.
St. Jerome, the great 5 th -century biblical scholar, identified the king with the Heavenly Father, the bridegroom as Jesus, and the bride as the Church.
The Pope said we too are involved in the story, as we belong to the Church and are chosen by the Lord to share our lives with Him and His life with others.
âThe wedding feast is ours, and the banquet hall is our churches and homes, the places where we live and where the Kingâs Son, Jesus Christ, continues to declare His love for us and await our âyesâ,â he said.
In conclusion, Pope Leo XIV pointed out that Christian joy is not artificial but âprofound, concrete, and real.â
Our joy, he said, âis as beautiful as the faces of the people we meet. It is as genuine as the work, the smiles, the tears, the handshakes, and the acts of kindness that fill our days. It is a gift of God for the salvation of the world.â
Thank you for reading our article. You can keep up-to-date by subscribing to our daily newsletter. Just click here .
The Angelus is a special prayer recited by Catholics three times a day, at 6am, noon, and 6pm and is accompanied by the ringing of the Angelus bell. The name comes from the Latin word for Angel and the prayer itself reminds us of how Jesus Christ assumed our human nature through the Mystery of the Incarnation. The Pope recites the Angelus prayer in St Peterâs Square every Sunday at midday. He also gives a brief reflection on the Gospel of the day and often comments on some issue of international concern. The Popeâs words are broadcast all over the world on radio and television and widely shared on social media. From Easter to Pentecost the Regina Coeli is prayed instead of the Angelus. This prayer commemorates the Resurrection of Jesus Christ and, like the Angelus, concludes with the recitation of the Gloria three times.

articles.title_orig: Puerto Vallarta boards up as Hurricane Simon hits Category 4 strength
articles.title_zh: Puerto Vallarta boards up as Hurricane Simon hits Category 4 strength
articles.content_orig:
Even after Hurricane Isaias plowed into the western Florida Panhandle on Friday night, causing widespread but non-catastrophic damage, the work of the NOAA/NWS National Hurricane Center was far from over. In an unprecedented onslaught, NHC found itself on Friday issuing advisories not only for Isaias but also for the U.S. Pacific coast and two stretches of Mexico’s Pacific coast, ahead of the projected weekend landfalls of Tropical Storm Rachel and Hurricane Simon. Both Rachel and Simon could produce significant, far-flung impacts, but in quite different ways.
Simon is by far the stronger of the two. After forming on Wednesday well offshore from Manzanillo, Mexico, Simon drifted westward as a tropical storm through Thursday night, then swung north while rapidly strengthening into a Category 4 hurricane on Friday and Friday night. As of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday , Simon was centered about 100 miles south-southwest of Manzanillo, heading north at 5 mph (7 km/h) with top sustained winds holding at 150 mph (240 km/h). Update : Yet another burst of strengthening pushed Simon’s top winds to 155 mph (260 km/h), just shy of Category 5 strength, as of 1 1 p.m. EDT Saturday . Simon was centered about 65 miles south-southwest of Manzanillo and was sliding northward at just 5 mph (7 km/h). As discussed below, it remains unclear whether the angle of this northward track will push Simon just inland, keep the hurricane just offshore, or hug the coast as the storm proceeds toward the general vicinity of Puerto Vallarta.
10/10 – Hurricane #Simon is nearing Category 5 intensity off SW #Mexico . Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast over the next few days, bringing life-threatening surf and rip currents. More: https://t.co/Wk7xxBl094 #marinewx #GOESEast pic.twitter.com/LE1Spow8ut
The first hurricane-hunter flight into Simon at midday Saturday confirmed the storm’s Cat 4 power, finding an estimated central pressure of 933 mb and peak flight-level winds of 153 mph (246 km/h). The storm’s tiny eye on Friday night allowed for ferociously quick strengthening, followed by an apparent eyewall replacement cycle that gave Simon a larger eyewall and a somewhat broader wind field. The hurricane hunters found concentric eyewalls roughly 14 and 41 miles (23 and 66 km) in diameter.
#Now #Hurricane #Simon disrupts 11 airports. All commercial flights canceled at #Manzanillo ; @flyVolaris suspends services at #PuertoVallarta , #Colima , #Tepic & #Uruapan . @Aeromexico & @flyVolaris announce passenger protections. https://t.co/xk9yQ6AqcH
Simon’s general north to north-northwest motion was expected to continue, with weak but steady steering currents holding in place until the hurricane nears the coast of northern Jalico state on Sunday. That’s where the track and intensity forecast become unusually tricky, because Simon will be approaching the coast at a near-parallel angle, with the storm’s stronger right-hand (east) side closer to the coast. This means that only a slight leftward or rightward deviation in the track can produce dramatically different impacts along and near the coast. There was little help from Saturday’s forecast models in pinpointing those impacts, because the model suites included everything from tracks that keep Simon just offshore through Monday to coast-scraping solutions to tracks that move Simon bodily inland on Sunday well south of Puerto Vallarta.
Since hurricanes interact with the rugged coastal terrain of this area, they often angle further east than models expect, as NHC noted , so it’s safest to assume that Simon will move onto the coastline at some point this weekend. The rugged terrain, and drying from downslope winds flowing offshore into Simon, may induce some weakening prior to landfall, but Simon will likely be a formidable storm regardless.
As shown in Fig. 1 above, the official forecast track as of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday brings the center of Simon onto the southern Jalisco coast as a major hurricane early Sunday afternoon, and in the vicinity of Puerto Vallarta as a weakening minimal hurricane on Sunday night, likely slowing and dissipating by Tuesday. Note that the “cone” in this graphic is based on average forecast error over the past five years, and is designed to include about two-thirds of possible tracks. Simon could remain much stronger for longer if it stays just offshore, possibly bringing significant wind impacts to a longer stretch of coastline. Or it could weaken more quickly than expected if it angles further inland after landfall.
Regardless of these track possibilities, Simon’s heaviest rains will likely be well south of Puerto Vallarta, with totals near the coast as high as 12-16 inches in parts of Jalisco, Colima, and Michoacán states. The torrential rains could lead to life-threatening flash floods and mudlides. Huge surf and swells and strong rip currents are also expected, while the biggest wind impacts will hinge more closely on wherever the eastern and northern eyewall end up moving onshore.
A few hundred miles north of Simon’s encounter with the Mexican coastline, sprawling Tropical Storm Rachel will sweep onshore early Sunday, its center passing just south of the U.S.–Mexico border. As of 5 p.m. EDT Saturday , resilient Rachel’s top sustained winds were at 65 mph, a bit stronger than on Friday, with some help from the upper-level trough pushing the storm along. Tropical-storm-force winds extended out up to 140 miles (220 km) from the center, making Rachel a even broader gale-producer than Simon. However, Rachel was producing only limited rainfall, as its banding features were largely devoid of intense showers and thunderstorms (see infrared satellite image at top). Update : At 11 p.m. EDT Saturday , ill-organized Rachel was reclassified as a post-tropical cyclone with top sustained winds of 60 mph (95 km/h). No major changes have been made to the overall outlook or the expected impacts through Sunday.
10/10 – Rachel is now a post-tropical cyclone, but that does not mean the threat has diminished. Strong winds, heavy rain, and dangerous swells will continue to affect Baja California and the southwestern United States. More: https://t.co/Wk7xxBl094 #marinewx #GOESWest pic.twitter.com/cXlOHFybsM
Given Rachel’s brisk northeast motion (about 22 mph or 35 km/h on Saturday afternoon) and the size of its wind field, the storm could be packing sustained winds in the 40-50 mph range on Sunday across far northwest Mexico and as far inland as southeast California and southwest Arizona. By late Sunday, Post-Tropical Storm Rachel (or its remnant circulation) will be racing northward through Utah. Even as the surface winds spin down, upper-level winds will be slower to do so, and powerful gusts could occurs across the higher terrain of the Southwest into Sunday afternoon and evening.
A Haboob/Dust Storm with winds up to 55Mph spawned by Tropical Storm Rachel just went through Riverside County California. #CAwx #Rachel pic.twitter.com/Is1J9X4mpH
As Rachel moves onshore, the same frictional effects and higher terrain that will lead to its rapid demise as a tropical storm will help enhance rainfall. A corridor of 1-to-3-inch rains near Rachel’s path is expected on Sunday from the deserts of far southern California across the Las Vegas area and into southern Utah. Flash flooding could occur, especially where Rachel’s rains fall in narrow canyons and atop burn scars. Even if global warming is limited to 1.5 degrees Celsius, scientists warn China’s densely populated coastline faces flooding this century
They said gravitational shifts caused by shrinking Antarctic ice would redistribute water across the globe, causing higher ocean levels along China’s densely populated coastlines.
“Even if we limit warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius [2.7 degrees Fahrenheit], the Paris Agreement’s most ambitious goal, Antarctica still has a 92 per cent chance of losing mass this century,” said lead author Lin Yucheng, an assistant professor at City University of Hong Kong’s school of energy and environment.

articles.title_orig: Four Years In, $40 Trillion Up: Why This AI-Fueled Bull Market Has Room to Run
articles.title_zh: Four Years In, $40 Trillion Up: Why This AI-Fueled Bull Market Has Room to Run
articles.content_orig:
For investors who think they’ve missed out on AI, the best is yet to come. But first, there will be a notable correction.
Since March 2009, the S&P 500 has experienced five declines of roughly 20% or more. Most were followed by relatively quick recoveries, reinforcing the belief that “buying the dip” is a reliable long-term strategy. However, these declines occurred within a broader secular bull market, which is an important distinction.
Understanding the secular trend often matters more than stock picking, as even the very best stocks can see extended periods of volatility if the secular trend reverses. In this report, we compare the current bull market to secular trends going back over 150 years to show why it is an extreme outlier.
Precisely because this market is an extreme outlier, how investors position themselves over the next few years will be crucial, particularly in AI stocks. My firm, the I/O Fund, specializes in AI, and while past performance is not a guarantee of future results, our track record in AI stocks has been exceptional.
Below, we do what very few investors dare to do, which is share our game plan and explain why we believe this bull market has considerably more room to run. However, before the next leg higher begins, we expect a correction that will shake many investors out of the trade.
The current bull market has lasted 17 years, and history proves this is very rare. Typically, long secular bull markets are broken up by periods of consolidation; but for more than a decade, that has not been the case.
The data shows that going back as far as 1880, there have been seven secular bear markets. They lasted, on average, 6.7 years with an average drawdown of 52.7%.
By comparison, since 1880, the average secular bull market lasts 11.2 years, with an average gain of 675%.
Compare this to the current bull market, going for 17.4 years old and up 1,073%, as of September 2026. On both measures it is becoming an extreme outlier compared to the average. That alone calls for caution, because it suggests we are closer to the end of this secular trend than the beginning. However, late in the cycle doesn’t mean over, and the wave structure outlined below shows why.
The Elliott Wave pattern of the current secular advance supports this view. Since the 2009 low, the market has been tracing a standard five-wave pattern, which follows the same guidelines on all time frames.
Below are some data points to support this claim:
Regarding the last point just made, an ending diagonal is a common pattern in Elliott Wave analysis, and the most likely interpretation of where we are in the larger secular pattern that started in 2009. These patterns only show up at the beginning and end of a trend, and they have distinct characteristics: they are 5 wave patterns, have exceptional overlap, and tend to trace a trend channel.
With those features in mind, I am tracking two scenarios that best fit the current price action.
The bigger takeaways from this analysis are twofold:
The above count aligns with what we’ve been seeing across AI stocks over the past year. Many of our positions are showing technical setups that point to longer, secular uptrends, with the potential for years of upside despite periods of volatility. Below, we examine Memory stocks – one of the hottest trends in AI to see whether the charts support a continued uptrend.
The South Korean KOSPI, an index consisting of 942 stocks, just dropped 44% in less than one month. This is a remarkable move for a developed country’s broad market, and there were several dynamics that created an environment for this unprecedented drop, one of which is that 54% of the total allocation of the index was Samsung and SK Hynix.
Even with the extraordinary volatility that we saw in the South Korean markets, the uptrend in this economy appears to be incomplete. As one of the primary beneficiaries to the memory boom needed to scale AI, this makes sense from a narrative perspective, as there is no evidence the need for memory is over, especially as we move into the inference phase of AI.

The KOSPI hit the lower target where we typically see 4 th waves end. If this level breaks, we can still be in an extended 4 th wave decline which has ample room to drop and still maintain the integrity of the larger secular uptrend.
Micron is in direct, aggressive competition with Samsung and SK Hynix for HBM orders. Interestingly, it’s long-term chart resembles the South Korean Kospi, almost identically.
We cover AI setups in detail during our weekly webinars, including the key levels we’re watching and how we’re positioning the portfolio. Join the I/O Fund’s next webinar at 4:30 p.m. Eastern on Thursday to see what the charts are signaling for AI stocks. Join I/O Fund
This is an area of the AI stack that we are heavily overweight – just over 50% of our portfolio is tilted toward lesser-known names that are directly involved in solving the networking bottleneck in AI.
One name that we have been vocal about, which is up over 188% YTD as one of our top 3 positions, is Lumentum (LITE) . Like memory, LITE, which sits in the middle of the networking stack, appears to have several large swings in its future.
Our firm was one of the first to address the AI energy bottleneck in 2024 . As a result, the I/O Fund used a portion of the cash we raised in early 2025 to buy Bloom Energy (BE) on the April 2025 lows. This caused our firm to establish a 5% allocation at $16.88 that is currently up over 1600%.
Bloom Energy addresses a very different challenge in the AI infrastructure buildout than networking or memory, yet its technical chart is signaling a similar long-term opportunity. Our analysis suggests Bloom is in the middle of a large five-wave pattern, with the potential for several more years of upside before the cycle is complete.
On a shorter timeframe, the S&P 500 appears to be setting up for a high of some kind into this cycle window. We appear to be tracing a smaller diagonal into this window, as shown below.
The breakout to all-time highs has confirmed this patterns completion. At minimum, we would then expect a pullback to the 7,300–7,265 area. If 7,265 breaks, the next target is 7,000–6,683.
This alternative scenario is outlined in red and is simply a different way to count the bullish scenario. Instead of a very shallow wave 2 happening in early June, which is what the green count is listing, we would be in that wave 2 once the 7265 support breaks. That would be uncomfortable, but as long as 6,683 holds, both outcomes would be pullbacks within a larger bullish uptrend. Below 6,683 and the odds will increase that we are setting up for the larger 4 th wave drop targeting sub-6000.
The important AI proxy in the broad semiconductor ETF (SMH) is confirming this risk. It is finishing a three-wave bounce on weak volume. Because the bounce made a lower high, it is best counted as a B wave in an ongoing correction, and not confirming the push higher in the S&P 500. A break below $541 would confirm this view, with a final target of $470–$430. A break above $640–$671.83 would invalidate the downside setup and point to a more bullish outcome sooner.
Our analysis of the AI investment cycle, combined with strength in the U.S. economy, suggests the secular bull market has another 1-3 years to run. While the current cycle is mature, we believe some of the strongest gains may still be ahead. We will especially watch key levels, such as 6,683 on the S&P 500 to ensure our strategy remains unchanged.
However, the path will not be without volatility. A strengthening U.S. dollar could tighten global liquidity conditions, which we will review in next week’s article. We would view that weakness as a potential buying opportunity, particularly for lesser-known AI stocks, which we cover weekly in our 1-hour webinars held every Thursday at 4:30 p.m. Eastern.

articles.title_orig: Back in Bushong: Brothers and World War II veterans Jay and William Moreland returned to their home and family eight decades after their deaths
articles.title_zh: Back in Bushong: Brothers and World War II veterans Jay and William Moreland returned to their home and family eight decades after their deaths
articles.content_orig:
The Moreland brothers have been returned home.
Repatriation activities took place Saturday afternoon for brothers Sgt. Jay Moreland and Staff Sgt. William Moreland of Bushong, beginning with a ceremony and presentation from the Morelands’ youngest brother, Larry Moreland, inside Robert’s-Blue-Barnett Funeral Home. Following the presentation, the brothers received a formal escort from Emporia to Bushong, where they were laid to rest with full military honors.
Following the ceremony, Larry Moreland spoke with KVOE News and said it was important to him and his family to hold a funeral ceremony for his brothers.
Moreland noted that he was, to an extent, surprised by the ceremony’s size and turnout.
The Moreland Brothers enlisted in the US Army in February 1943 and, at their request, trained and deployed together as members of the 149th Engineer Combat Battalion. The brothers died on June 6th, 1944, during the invasion of Omaha Beach on D-Day when their landing craft struck an underwater German mine.
Jay Moreland was 21 and William 19 at the time of their deaths. Larry Moreland, who was only an infant at the time of his siblings’ passing, says their military careers were indicative of how “inseparable” his brothers were throughout their lives.
As mentioned, Saturday’s ceremony was a largely attended affair by both residents and veterans, including a half-dozen chapters of the American Legion Riders who helped provide the brothers’ escort, alongside local law enforcement. American Legion Post 5 member Clay Childs says this turnout symbolizes the unity and camaraderie amongst military personnel regardless of their branch of service.
Saturday’s ceremony was the second repatriation ceremony for a native of Bushong after Sgt. John Owen Herrick was laid to rest back in 2024. Herrick was also a member of the 149th Engineer Combat Battalion and died aboard the same craft as the Moreland brothers in 1944.
Click here for a YouTube Short recapping the Moreland Brothers’ repatriation.
Photos by Tagan Trahoon/KVOE News.

articles.title_orig: 'Take that light into the world': Interfaith group holds candlelight vigil for peace
articles.title_zh: 'Take that light into the world': Interfaith group holds candlelight vigil for peace
articles.content_orig:
In the shadow of a war memorial, a group of residents rallied for peace.
Wareham Faith in Action, an interfaith organization that works with Wareham Law and Democracy, gathered people at Center Park for its first peace vigil on Saturday, Oct. 10.
Vigil goers lit candles and listened to speeches and songs that called for an end to wars overseas and ICE detentions at home.
“Peace doesn’t mean the absence of tension, but it means the presence of justice,” said Wandra Harmsen in a speech. “And when we have justice, we will have peace.”
The vigil’s message was "Light a candle. Hold a hope. Stand for peace." Wareham Faith in Action organizers gave candles to everyone in attendance and had people light each other’s candles, spreading the flame throughout the park.
“We’ll ask you to take that light into the world,” Wareham Faith in Action Co-Chair Lisa Govoni told the attendees.
Those who attended had a common goal: change. “We’re here for change,” said Maria Rowley. “Justice and equality for all.”
“Our country needs a little boost of peace,” said Candy Johansen.
The Golden Rule was a core theme of the vigil. Keith Harvey, another co-chair and a Quaker, said that many of the world’s religions include some form of the rule directing people to treat everyone fairly. He said that Wareham Faith in Action wanted to bring people of all faiths together through their common beliefs.
The organization didn’t allow political messaging at the vigil. Harvey said that the organization keeps politics out of its events in order to bring more people in.
“There’s a center that all faiths are trying to move to. Let’s move there together,” Harvey said.
Henry St. Julien, a Wareham resident and the director of diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging at the Falmouth School District, talked about Anthony Burns, a slave who escaped to Boston but was arrested and returned to Virginia in 1854 under the Fugitive Slave Act. He said that 50,000 Bostonians protested the detention, shaming the officers arresting Burns.
He also said that a group of Bostonians raised thousands of dollars to buy Burns’ freedom.
St. Julien drew parallels between Burns’ story and the stories of families who have been detained and deported by ICE.
“History … it’s a mirror,” St. Julien said. “When we look at this mirror, we see a reoccurring history … where there’s a struggle for human dignity against systems.”
He said that as a school administrator, he needs to come up with a plan to help students in case their parents are detained. He said he’s seen fear creep into his schools.
“I’m compelled by my faith,” he said. “And every day, I ensure that every child walks through our doors, feels safe, seen, valued and protected, regardless of where they’re born, what language they speak … what status they have.”
St. Julien urged the vigil goers not to let their work end after the event. He said they should continue to make their voices heard. “Chaos flourishes when good people stay silent while vulnerable [people] are targeted,” he said.
Wareham Faith in Action gave attendees ways to help, promoting a GoFundMe to support Haitian families living in the area who had their temporary protected statuses removed over the summer.
The organization will continue hosting events promoting peace. It already hosted three peace walks this summer.
Harmsen said that the organization will “aim higher” with its coming events and try to involve local government and other parts of the community.

North Carolina Emergency Management activated Mooresville Fire-Rescue’s Swift Water Rescue team to western North Carolina, with 12 Mooresville Fire-Rescue members deploying to Yancey County.

articles.title_orig: Kalen DeBoer talks refs, injuries and more after Alabama loses to Georgia
articles.title_zh: Kalen DeBoer talks refs, injuries and more after Alabama loses to Georgia
articles.content_orig:
OutKick's Trey Wallace provides an update on the weather after Hurricane Isaias' remnants made its way through Tuscaloosa ahead of Saturday's Alabama-Georgia game.
TUSCALOOSA, AL- Don't tell Georgia or Alabama that Saturday night's game in Tuscaloosa was meaningless because of the current college football playoff format.
After a week full of drama surrounding Hurricane Isaias and whether we would see these two teams take the field on time, fans were treated to a heavyweight showdown inside Bryant Denny Stadium on Saturday in front of a soaked crowd watching from the stands.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
We did not need any extra hype for this one. The theatrical movies that schools release before kickoff were not going to do anything that the Bulldogs and Tide couldn’t do when they arrived around 5:40 p.m. EST on Saturday afternoon.
WATCH AS OUTKICK'S TREY WALLACE BRAVES HURRICANE ISAIAS' BEFORE ALABAMA-GEORGIA SHOWDOWN IN TUSCALOOSA
This was about Kirby Smart trying to buck the regular season trend against Alabama, while Kalen DeBoer looked to put his team back into the perceived national spot that some wanted to argue they had fallen out of.
What you got was two teams trading haymakers for a first half that ended with DeBoer going for a touchdown with just seconds remaining on the clock, taking a 14-10 lead into the locker room.
ALABAMA PROVIDES UPDATE FOR SHOWDOWN AGAINST GEORGIA, AS SCHOOL, SEC AND TRUMP PLAN FOR HURRICANE ISAIAS
This came after Georgia had found its way out of its own end of the field on two occasions for 10 points.
Running back EJ Crowell of the Alabama Crimson Tide gets around defensive back KJ Bolden of the Georgia Bulldogs for a touchdown during the first half at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa, Ala., on Oct. 10, 2026. (Getty Images)
A late-arriving crowd inside a a misty Bryant Denny Stadium watched two coaches trying to outmaneuver each other for four quarters, while Keelon Russell and Gunner Stockton traded shots on offense.
What more could you ask for on a day filled with so much drama around college football?
Heck, in the fourth quarter alone this evening, Georgia missed a field goal that would have given it the lead against Alabama, while Kentucky missed a 26-yard chip shot that would have tied the game with LSU.
There were plenty of times in this game tonight where Georgia felt like the better football team, in all facets. But then, when you have such dynamic team like Alabama that can score on you within seconds, no lead seemed safe.
In reality, we were watching two of the best teams in college football in Tuscaloosa, and it doesn’t matter that they both come from the SEC. You can add Ohio State to that list, while taking Texas off of it at the same time.
Head coach Kirby Smart of the Georgia Bulldogs reacts after a penalty during the first half against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Oct. 10, 2026, in Tuscaloosa, Ala. (Getty Images)
We are reaching that point in the season where the frauds are starting to show themselves, and there wasn’t one on the field in Tuscaloosa. We can talk about Alabama and this team moving past the Saban era until we're blue in the face, and some will still be doing 10 years from now.
ALABAMA CRIMSON TIDE NAMES STARTER FOR WEEK ONE: GET TO KNOW BAMA QUARTERBACK KEELON RUSSELL
While Georgia would retake the lead with a field goal on the ensuing drive, the officials would become part of the story late in the fourth quarter.
Chaos reigned on Alabama's drive, as Georgia was not called for an obvious pass interference that would have resulted in the Tide extending its drive by 15-yards. But, as the boos reigned down from the Bryant Denny Stadium stands, there was nothing left for the Alabama fans to cheer about after the Bulldogs sacked Keelon Russell on the ensuing play.
In that moment, tacked on with a personal foul against Dijon Lee that resulted in Georgia being able to take a knee and run the clock out, which once led to Kalen DeBoer being the most animated we've seen him during his time at Alabama.
Until somebody beats them, it's the Dawgs .
One way or the other, Kirby Smart has a football team that finds a way to win football games, which is not the case for other teams across the Southeastern Conference , or the sport.
"I didn’t come here to lose," Kirby Smart said after the game.
We witnessed a football team fighting through adversity, with the world wondering if Kirby Smart was going to get over some type of perceived hump.
Head coach Kirby Smart of the Georgia Bulldogs reacts during the second quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Bryant-Denny Stadium on Sept. 28, 2024, in Tuscaloosa, Ala. (Getty Images)
The problem for those pushing that message: Kirby Smart really does not care any longer. Following the win, Smart bolted straight for the visitors section, slinging his visor around in the air while the Georgia fans and Kirby's wife waited to embrace his family.
"I'd rather make memories with my family, team and coaching staff ... I just wanted to celebrate with my wife..She deserved a kiss for all that she puts up with from me."
We are witnessing a new Kirby Smart, who is not worried about trying to silence critics or whatever is being written about him.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
That's a dangerous man, who seems to be fighting more for the respect from his family and those who encompass the football facility in Athens.
"Do I wanna win championships? Hell yeah, but I have a lot more respect for them (family and players) to understand that there's a lot more important things in life."
Welcome to the new era of Kirby Smart.
Trey Wallace is the Sr. College Sports Reporter for OutKick.

articles.title_orig: MacBook Pro overhaul: entry-level model to gain new design sooner than expected
articles.title_zh: MacBook Pro overhaul: entry-level model to gain new design sooner than expected
articles.content_orig:
Earlier this year, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman revealed that Apple has a new M7-powered entry level MacBook Pro in the pipeline for spring 2027. This isn’t an ordinary MacBook Pro refresh though. It’ll bring the upcoming redesign down to the entry level, something that previously wasn’t expected.
Normally, when Apple introduces a new MacBook Pro design, it takes a while to trickle down. For instance, the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M1 Pro and M1 Max was introduced in 2021, but the base model MacBook Pro stuck with the 13-inch design until 2023, when it gained the 14-inch chassis with the M3 chip .
Similarly, when Apple redesigned the MacBook Pro in 2016, it wasn’t until 2019 that the entry level model gained the Touch Bar. There’s also a similar story for the 2012 retina MacBook Pro redesign.
This time around though, there’ll only be a roughly 6 month gap before the redesign comes to the entry level.
According to Bloomberg , Apple will be introducing the redesign to the entry level MacBook Pro in early 2027, shortly after debuting it in the high end MacBook Pros, rumored to be called MacBook Ultra. From the report :
Apple is also preparing a revamped entry-level MacBook Pro, code-named K104, for as early as the first half of next year. The 14-inch laptop will adopt a new design in line with what Apple is preparing for higher-end MacBooks with touch screens due between the end of this year and early next year.
It’s worth noting that there’ll also be another entry level MacBook Pro with the current design and the M6 chip, which is currently on track to debut this fall alongside the redesigned high-end MacBook Pros.
To make things even weirder, those redesigned high-end MacBook Pros are also expected to debut with the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, instead of M6 generation chips. Apple recently made a decision to abandon its plans for high end M6 chips to instead accelerate M7.
In short, it’ll look like this:
Of course, the redesign is expected to feature a slightly thinner chassis, OLED displays with touch support, and possibly even come with a Dynamic Island.
With the recent price hikes, this is excellent news for some people. I’m sure the redesigned 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro will likely cost over $2500, so if you’re looking to get something more in budget with the M7 chip and the redesign, you’ll only have to wait until the following spring.
I wish Apple would come back to the lines up it had years ago, one restyling of all the laptops, one of all the ipad at the same time and so on, in the last few years they have be releasing updates bits at the time, sometime the line up doesn't even make sense (M4 pro next to Basic M5). If i need to finally update a machine I'm stuck between waiting for a never arriving hardware or buying something already old. it really doesn't make sense. the only thing they kept similar is the iPhone line up each year where they change all the models at the same time, although they have the occasional basic model popping up here and there... also the've become very slow in their release, by the time a new ipad comes out there are already rumors and specs about the next model... it really doesn`t make sense commercially....
It’s certainly unfortunate that the $1,999 price point of the entry level MacBook Pro today is what the Pro chip versions cost just under a year ago , but that’s the inevitable reality of this memory shortage .

articles.title_orig: World Mental Health Day
articles.title_zh: World Mental Health Day
articles.content_orig:
Dr Nilesh Buddha, Officer-in-Charge, WHO South-East Asia
Around the world, more than 1 billion people live with a mental health condition – most commonly anxiety or depression – and suicide remains a leading cause of death of young people. In the WHO South-East Asia Region, 208 000 people are lost each year to suicide, and an estimated 289 million people live with a mental, neurological, self-harm, or substance use condition.
This year, the theme of World Mental Health Day, “ Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change ,” reminds us that people with lived experience (PWLE) of mental health conditions must not only be recipients of care – their voices must help shape the care, policies, and services that affect their lives. PWLE are a source of knowledge and expertise, and a powerful force for change, helping challenge stigma and discrimination, and helping services become more responsive, respectful, and relevant. When PWLE participate as equal partners, mental health systems move closer to putting people first.
The Region has made progress. India has launched a nationwide tele-mental health initiative, and Bangladesh and Nepal are advancing WHO's Special Initiative for Mental Health . Bhutan and Sri Lanka are expanding community services, and Maldives is strengthening suicide prevention. Myanmar has reinforced psychosocial support, and Thailand is pioneering digital tools and workforce development. In 2025, the WHO South-East Asia Region launched a dashboard on mental, neurological, substance use, and self-harm conditions, to help accelerate and strengthen evidence-based planning, monitoring, and evaluation of mental health services and policies.
In 2024, WHO convened a mental health summit, “ Voices of People with Lived Experience in the WHO South-East Asia Region, ” in Nepal. PWLE and caregivers from eight countries shared perspectives on their rights, including access to health care, employment, housing, and education, and to identify opportunities for policy and systems reform. The resulting Kathmandu Charter for the Rights of People with Lived Experience of Mental Health Conditions is a guide for Member States to develop contextualized national charters of their own. It sets out rights to equal opportunities, autonomy in decision-making, community-based care, and participation in development of policies, programmes, and budgets.
The Region is guided by the Paro Declaration on universal access to people-centred mental health care and services , adopted in 2022. It commits to reorient mental health services around primary health care, to establish rights-oriented community mental health networks, and to combat stigma and discrimination through community empowerment and the active engagement of PWLE. The regional Mental Health Action Plan 2023–2030 puts these commitments into practice, making the involvement of PWLE in policy development, implementation, service evaluation, and research agendas a guiding principle. It further calls on Member States to support independent organisations of PWLE, and establishes regional targets including a 50% increase in government service coverage for mental health conditions, and a 15% reduction in the suicide rate by 2030.
Nevertheless, gaps remain. In many Member States, treatment gaps are as high as 90%. Services are concentrated in urban areas and institutions, out-of-pocket expenditure is high, and stigma and discrimination are widespread. Universal access requires addressing stigma and discrimination, strengthening community participation, supporting families and caregivers, and ensuring that PWLE have a meaningful voice in the design, implementation and evaluation of mental health policies, services, and budgets.
WHO is committed to working with Member States, PWLE, families, caregivers, civil society, health workers, and communities across the Region to transform mental health care and support, building systems where every voice matters, every person is treated with dignity, and everyone can access the mental health care and support they need, when and where they need it.

articles.title_orig: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
articles.title_zh: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
articles.content_orig:
Middle East expert Behnam Ben Taleblu ties Houthi airport attacks to Iranian threats and warns of possible Russian involvement.
Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports .
The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.
SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE
Smoke and flames rise from King Khalid International Airport after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Oct. 8, 2026. (Reuters)
Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis.
"Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu , senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday.
"The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned.
RUBIO ACCUSES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES
Smoke was reported near King Khalid International Airport, seen above, as regional tensions and Houthi attacks heightened security concerns in Saudi Arabia. (AFP via Getty Images)
The Houthis also renewed warnings Sunday, urging airlines, airport workers and travelers to avoid Saudi airports as Saudi Arabia vowed to retaliate for the deadly attacks.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned Saturday's attack, confirming that an American was among those killed and calling for an immediate end to the violence.
President Donald Trump, meanwhile, left open the possibility of U.S. involvement in Saudi Arabia's military campaign against the Houthis, saying, "We may. We're gonna look at it. We move very quickly."
The escalation comes nearly three weeks after a senior Iranian official threatened to paralyze neighboring countries' airports if they cooperated with U.S. efforts to restrict Iranian flights.
THE HOUTHIS AREN'T SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM. AMERICA CAN'T AFFORD TO LOOK AWAY
Mohsen Rezaei was named secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. A former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps general and member of the Expediency Discernment Council, as well as the secretary of the Supreme Council for Economic Coordination and the Iranian government's Economic Committee, attends a ceremony at Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini's shrine in southern Tehran, Iran, on June 4, 2026. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto)
Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned Sept. 23 that Iran would prevent neighboring countries' airports from operating if they cooperated with Washington's efforts to restrict Iranian flights, according to Reuters .
"This rapid targeting reflects earlier threats made by Iranian officials, including a veiled threat from the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warning that U.S. sanctions on Iran's aviation sector would lead to retaliatory threats against neighboring aviation infrastructure," Taleblu said.
Iran has long supported the Houthis, but the extent of Tehran's involvement in the latest airport attacks has not been independently established.
The escalation has also renewed scrutiny of reports that Russia has provided intelligence and technical assistance to the Houthis.
FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT
Yemen's Houthi armed forces patrol as Yemeni prisoners loyal to the Houthis arrive in the capital of Sanaa on Sept. 12, 2026, after being released on the west coast where they had been held by Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces. (AFP via Getty Images)
At a Sept. 1 House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing , lawmakers pressed experts on allegations that Russia is providing intelligence and technical support to the Houthis.
"Beyond offering diplomatic cover, there are persistent reports of Russian satellite collaboration, advisory support, and intelligence targeting assistance, as well as unproven allegations regarding select anti-ship systems."
HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS
Yemen's Iran-backed armed Houthi group has warned they will move to shutter the Bab Al-Mandeb Strait through missile-drone attacks if Gulf nations join the US-Israel war on Iran. (Mohammed Hamoud/Getty Images)
But he also linked the latest attacks to a broader military escalation as the Houthis expand their territorial control in Yemen.
"This surge did not occur in a vacuum," Taleblu said. "Since April, the Houthis have made territorial gains and pushed back against Saudi forces despite a period of diplomatic lull."

"Airport attacks allow Iran and its regional proxies to inflict pain on Arab states, Israel, and remaining U.S. forces," Taleblu said.

articles.title_orig: Mainland condemns Taiwan leader for playing up 'mainland threat'
articles.title_zh: Mainland condemns Taiwan leader for playing up 'mainland threat'
articles.content_orig:
The Chinese mainland on Saturday condemned Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te for clinging to a "Taiwan independence" stance and playing up the so-called mainland threat in a speech, saying his remarks misled the public and fueled confrontation across the Taiwan Strait.
Zhang Han, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said Lai's speech disregarded facts, distorted right and wrong, and exposed his ulterior motives, revealing his true colors as a so-called pragmatic worker for Taiwan independence.
ALSO READ: Mainland criticizes Taiwan authorities over 'defense' spending increase
Zhang criticized Lai for stubbornly adhering to a separatist "Taiwan independence" stance and playing up the so-called mainland threat. She also accused him of promoting the false narrative of "democracy versus authoritarianism" and seeking "Taiwan independence" through force and by relying on external forces.
Such moves stoke confrontation across the Taiwan Strait and undermine regional peace and stability, Zhang said.
"There is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is part of China," Zhang said, stressing that this remains the real status quo across the Taiwan Strait. She added that the one-China principle is a basic norm governing international relations, a broad consensus in the international community and an important part of the post-World War II international order.
READ MORE: Mainland slams DPP authorities for blocking job site serving Taiwan youth
"The future of Taiwan can only and must be decided jointly by all Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots," she said.
Zhang said the mainland would uphold the one-China principle and the 1992 Consensus, unite people from all walks of life in Taiwan, resolutely combat separatist forces seeking "Taiwan independence", oppose external interference, and safeguard peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.
"As people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait are one family, we will deepen cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, promote the peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations, and advance the cause of national reunification and rejuvenation," she added.

After spending all her savings on a month-long trip to Antarctica following a cancer diagnosis, a woman from southwestern China discovered that her tumour had shrunk.
Wang Ying, 67, is an amateur wildlife photographer who has photographed more than 1,200 bird species.

articles.title_orig: Impact of Isaias: Officials confirm 2 storm-related deaths in Florida, 430K without power
articles.title_zh: Impact of Isaias: Officials confirm 2 storm-related deaths in Florida, 430K without power
articles.content_orig:
Hurricane Isaias made landfall in the late evening of Oct. 9 in the Florida Panhandle at Category 2 strength.
Wind gusts over 110 mph were clocked in several panhandle locations, along with storm surge flooding. Over 700,000 customers are without power in its wake.
Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, Friday evening with sustained winds of 105 mph, a Category 2 hurricane.
That was the first hurricane to landfall in the mainland U.S. in exactly two years, since Milton slammed into western Florida on Oct. 9, 2024.
A rarely-issued extreme wind warning was issued Friday evening for the western Florida Panhandle, including Pensacola and Destin, for the likelihood of wind gusts over 115 mph ahead of the eyewall of Isaias.
The highest gust recorded was 116 mph in Santa Rosa Sound, Florida, where sustained winds of 91 mph were also measured.
Set The Weather Company as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.
Pensacola reported a 102-mph wind gust earlier Friday evening. Gulf Breeze, Florida, located across Pensacola Bay from Pensacola, reported a wind gust of 97 mph and sustained winds of 83 mph.
Early observations show water levels surpassed 4.0 feet above normally dry ground in Destin and 5.6 feet in Panama City, Florida, and were likely higher in the western Panhandle.
One caveat with these storm surge totals is they are measured relative to the Mean Higher High Water (MHHW) and this number includes tide influences so they should not be interpreted as storm surge heights alone.
The highest wind gust reported was an impressive 117 mph three miles east-southeast of Oriole Beach. Two miles west southwest of Pensacola, at City Hall, a gust of 102 was reported.
There was a roof blown off the Rest and Relax Inn on Plantation Road in Pensacola. Multiple collapsed gas station canopies were reported in Pensacola (Blue Angel Parkway and Mobile Highway) and also in Crestview. Trees were uprooted, one of which crushed a business on Fort Walton Beach. There were also multiple RVs blown over, including one onto US 98 between Gulf Breeze and Navarre.
Less than 12 hours prior to landfall, an instrumented NOAA Saildrone measured a gust of 104 mph near the eyewall of Isaias, according to the National Hurricane Center.
In Alabama, a gust of 75 mph was reported near Orange Beach while Birmingham saw a gust of 49 mph.
Trees fell directly onto residences in Mountain Brook, Birmingham (Five Points & Ensley), Opelika (manufactured home), and Ladonia (tree through a house).
All roads were impassable in Conecuh County due to debris and fallen trees.
Georgia saw a 68 mph gust in Warner Robins while Hartsfield-Jackson Airport saw a gust to 45 mph.
In terms of heavy rainfall, Bellwood, Alabama, saw over a foot of rain in just 13 hours. Caney Creek/FAWN Station, Florida, saw 12.06 inches in 24 hours, with 9.67 falling in 3 hours and 4.15 inches falling in 1 hour.
Flash flooding reports were observed at Westland Apartments in Bellair, Florida, while flash flooding stranded a vehicle in floodwaters near Sale City, Georgia.
In Florida, Bayside Subdivision and Destin saw 7.18 inches and 7.52 inches of rainfall, respectively. The Greater Atlanta area saw 1-3 inches of rainfall in a 6 hour period early Saturday.
A flash flood warning was even in effect for part of Atlanta that morning.
And on Saturday, multiple tornadoes were sighted by storm spotters in the Savannah River Valley including near Newington and Oliver, Georgia.
There were also multiple tornado reports across South Carolina on Saturday. Near Appleton, South Carolina, four homes were severely damaged, as well as numerous trees and powerlines down. Barnwell County Aiken County, and Newberry County also had reports of tornadoes.
On Oct. 11, remnants of Isaias moved into North Carolina, producing heavy rainfall, flash flooding and landslides.
A few tornadoes were also reported in North Carolina, near Candor, Clarendon and Atkinson, North Carolina.
Numerous flood watches and warnings were also issued across Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania on Oct. 11.
Isaias replaced "Ike" on one of the Atlantic name lists after that name was retired following the destructive, deadly 2008 hurricane .
It wasn't used during its first year of eligibility in 2014, since we only reached the eighth name, Hanna, that year.
However, the name was used in 2020 for a storm that eventually tracked up the East Coast with destructive winds.

articles.title_orig: Rumor: Apple to Announce New Partnership With ADT
articles.title_zh: Rumor: Apple to Announce New Partnership With ADT
articles.content_orig:
Apple may be planning to announce a new partnership with home security company ADT, alongside the introduction of its all-new smart home hub , according to several clues. Apple has invited the media to a "Welcome home" experience in New York on Tuesday, October 13 , so the partnership could be made official on that day.
Since around July, ADT has posted "Low Voltage Technician" job listings in various U.S. cities, but those hired for the position so far have been provided with very few details about their specific responsibilities. In recent months, some of these people said they have primarily been shadowing other ADT technicians while they await further information. In addition, some of the employees and their managers said they signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) related to the role. This high level of secrecy is very common for Apple.
Another potential giveaway is that ADT has provided these new hires with iPhones for work, whereas its other technicians have received Android devices.
A third clue is that some of the new hires said ADT finally plans to share more details about the role later this month, so the company may be waiting for Apple to announce its smart home hub on Tuesday. Apple is also expected to unveil an ecosystem of third-party smart home accessories it developed in partnership with brands such as LG .
One of the new hires said ADT initially planned to provide details about the role in September, but later delayed this timeframe until October. This would be consistent with reports that Apple has postponed the announcement of its home hub multiple times, as Siri AI was not ready. The revamped version of Siri finally launched last month.
In addition to Siri AI, the home hub will reportedly offer smart home accessory management, home security monitoring, photo faces and galleries, an overview of calendar appointments, music playback, FaceTime video calling, and more. The hub will reportedly be available in a tabletop version with a speaker base and a wall-mounted version.
Some of the new hires who asked their managers about the secretive role were told that it will apparently relate to home automation and in-home installation services, so perhaps Apple will announce an option for customers to have an ADT technician professionally install the wall-mounted home hub or the related accessories from LG.
It is unclear if Apple's partnership with ADT would extend to home security monitoring.
ADT already reached a home security partnership with Google in 2023 , but it reportedly dropped some features that it offered on Google Nest devices earlier this year. A few people familiar with the matter told us that ADT's agreement with Google either already expired this year or will expire next year and is not set to be renewed. If this is true, then it would pave the way for ADT to reach a partnership with another tech giant: Apple.
Keep in mind that a potential partnership between Apple and ADT is still just a rumor for now, and all of these clues could somehow prove to be one big coincidence. But if the partnership does become official on Tuesday, you heard it here first.

articles.title_orig: Shooter kills 8 people and himself in Pennsylvania, police say, with Governor Shapiro offering support
articles.title_zh: Shooter kills 8 people and himself in Pennsylvania, police say, with Governor Shapiro offering support
articles.content_orig:
A man killed eight people and himself during a mass shooting at a house in Erie, Pennsylvania, local police said Saturday.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said seven of the eight victims were related to the shooter, with the eighth person being a family friend. The shooter had died of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound before authorities arrived at the scene.
Among the victims was a 1-year-old girl and 5-year-old boy, with a pregnant woman also dead in the shooting.
"Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said, describing an "eerie silence" when police arrived at the home.
The identity of the 45-year-old shooter has not yet been revealed by authorities. The motive for the massacre is also still unclear, with police pursuing an investigation .
At a press conference, Erie Mayor Daria Devlin addressed the families of the victims.
"I am so deeply sorry. What happened to you was horrific, and there is nothing that any of us can say today that will make this any easier," she said. "But you do need to know that our entire community is with you, we're grieving with you. And we are here to support you."
Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro spoke with Devlin by phone and offered his support to Erie.
"I've spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my administration's full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians," Shapiro said in a statement post on X.
Shapiro said his "heart breaks for this family" and added that he and his wife Lori Shapiro "are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community."
Shapiro, a Democrat , has pushed for gun control bills in his state and signed an executive order in 2024 to reestablish the Pennsylvania Office of Gun Violence Prevention.

articles.title_orig: Alabama vs. Georgia live updates: No. 6 Crimson Tide meet No. 2 Bulldogs in pivotal SEC showdown
articles.title_zh: Alabama vs. Georgia live updates: No. 6 Crimson Tide meet No. 2 Bulldogs in pivotal SEC showdown
articles.content_orig:
Two of the SEC's three remaining undefeated teams will battle it out Saturday night inside Bryant-Denny Stadium.
No. 2 Georgia is a 2.5-point underdog on the road at No. 6 Alabama (7:30 p.m. ET on ABC). All week attention centered on the potential impact of Hurricane Isaias on the night game between the two SEC heavyweights. While central Alabama received plenty of rain overnight and through the afternoon, Isaias devolved into a post-tropical system by Saturday morning. The weather will likely have a more limited impact than was initially feared earlier in the week.
What we should see Saturday night is one of the most explosive offenses in the country versus one of the best defenses especially when it comes to stopping the run. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell has been terrific this season for the Crimson Tide, throwing for 1,1414 yards, 14 touchdowns and only two interceptions. His favorite target has been Ryan Coleman-Williams who leads the team with 376 receiving yards and four touchdowns.
Georgia has dominated all the competition it has faced this season but gets its toughest test yet against Alabama. He doesn't get as much attention as Russell, but Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton has been very good for the Bulldogs. He has 13 touchdowns to only one interception and has ably guided the UGA offense to big wins over opponents like Oklahoma and Vanderbilt. The Bulldogs are expected to have leading rusher Nate Frazier closer to full strength after missing most of the last two games.
Not only would the winner of this game be in prime early position to make the SEC Championship but would have a better than 93 percent chance to make the College Football Playoff, according to CBS Sports' forecasting and projections team.
Keep it locked here as CBS Sports provides you with live updates, highlights and analysis as Alabama battles Georgia on Saturday.
A tipped INT notwithstanding, Gunner Stockton is having himself a helluva game in Tuscaloosa. He's made multiple big-time throws tonight including a 30-yard one to Craig Dandridge that was right on the money in tight coverage. Stockton then kept it to himself and scored on a 14-yard run.
He's 11 for 13 for 188 yards, one passing touchdown, one rushing touchdown and an interception. That was a strong response from Georgia to start the second half after the way Alabama took the lead right before the half.
A gutsy decision from Kalen DeBoer right before halftime paid off as EJ Crowell raced in from a yard out to give No. 6 Alabama a 14-10 lead over No. 2 Georgia. The Bulldogs will start with the ball in the second half.
Facing a second-and-goal from Georgia's 1-yard line with only time for one more play, DeBoer opted to run the ball with Crowell, who was able to get the edge on a Georgia defender and run in for the touchdown. It was an impressive two-minute drive from Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell and the Crimson Tide offense after the defense stopped Georgia.
Georgia struck first off a 42-yard Peyton Woodring field goal in the first quarter for a 3-0 lead. The Bulldogs added to that with a Gunner Stockton to London Humphreys 20-yard touchdown pass. Stockton was efficient and effective in the first half, finishing 9 for 11 for 143 yards, one touchdown and an interception. Stockton set up the touchdown drive with a 53-yard pass to Jaden Reddell, who raced down the middle of the field.
Alabama wasn't able to muster as many explosive plays as fans have become accustomed to seeing this season, but finally broke through in the second quarter. Trae'shawn Brown gave Alabama the big play it desperately needed with a 58-yard run. One play later, Keelon Russell got Alabama on the board with a 22-yard touchdown pass to Marshall Pritchett. Russell didn't look particularly comfortable early on against the Bulldogs, but settled in nicely in the second quarter. He finished the half 11 for 22 for 119 yards, one touchdown and one lost fumble.
Alabama outgained Georgia, 224-192, in the first half.
Alabama's defense is facing a critical series here coming out of the two-minute timeout. Georgia is on its own 42-yard line with all three timeouts remaining and set up to get the ball to start the second half. Gunner Stockton has been moving the ball well. Georgia adding another touchdown right before halftime could be a backbreaker.
Alabama has had some success bringing extra pressure on Stockton. Can it dial it up a bit more to force a punt?
No team had more explosive plays than Alabama coming into tonight's game. Through the first quarter-and-a-half, though, Alabama couldn't manage much. And then came the big breakthrough on a Trae'shawn Brown 58-yard run. The very next play Keelon Russell connected with Marshall Pritchett for a 22-yard touchdown.
Georgia jumping out to a 10-0 lead quieted the crowd but two big plays back-to-back after the place roaring again.
Gunner Stockton threw a dart to Jaden Reddell who raced past a step-too-slow Bray Hubbard down the middle of the field for a 53-yard gain. The very next play Stockton hit London Humphreys for a 20-yard touchdown to give Georgia a two-score lead and completely quieted the Bryant-Denny Stadium crowd. Alabama had been doing a good job bottling up Georgia's offense before Stockton found something he liked down the middle.
Stockton is a perfect 6 for 6 for 109 yards and a touchdown.
It has turned into a defensive slugfest here in the first half. Georgia is all over Keelon Russell, who hasn't looked super comfortable early on in this one. He's 4 for 7 for 24 yards and a lost fumble. The big play opportunities Russell excelled at last week against Mississippi State haven't been there.
Similarly, Alabama's defense hasn't given Georgia much to work with. After a terrific Alabama punt was downed at Georgia's 3-yard line, the Bulldogs couldn't manage much and had to punt after a three-and-out. Gunner Stockton is 2 for 2 for 29 yards.
Despite the penalties, Georgia put three points on the board off a Peyton Woodring 43-yard field goal. Dwight Phillips had 16 rushing yards -- plus a 17-yard rushing touchdown that was called back -- while Gunner Stockton connected with Lawson Luckie for a 26-yard gain to power Georgia's early offense.
Georgia appeared to have the first points of the game on a Dwight Phillips touchdown run...until a holding penalty brought it back. It wasn't an egregious hold but was just enough right in front of an official to get called. On the next play, Georgia got hit for a rare offensive pass interference call on a pick play that resulted in an injury to Jaden Reddell.
If Georgia doesn't emerge with points from this drive, those penalties will loom extra large.
A promising first drive for Alabama ends when Keelon Russell gets hit from his blind side and fumbles the ball on Georgia's 37-yard line. Russell didn't have much of a shot with Joseph Jonah-Ajonye on him as quickly as he was. The Bulldogs get the ball on their 39-yard line.
We are just about to kick off here in Bryant-Denny Stadium. Georgia won the toss and has chosen to defer. It's been a rainy day in Alabama, and we'll see how it impacts Keelon Russell and this high-powered Alabama offense to start.
For all the incredible success Kirby Smart has had at Georgia, Alabama has remained a quandary he rarely has been able to figure out. Smart has a 122-21 record while at UGA, and yet seven of those 21 losses have come at the hands of the Crimson Tide. Smart beat Alabama in last season's SEC Championship -- his first win in four tries against Bama in Atlanta -- but has yet to win a regular-season game. Smart is 0-3 all-time against Alabama, with the last two coming in back-to-back seasons against Kalen DeBoer.
Can Kirby get his first regular-season win over Alabama tonight? His Bulldogs are 2.5-point underdogs on the road.

articles.title_orig: 26% in Japan see U.S. as biggest threat to world peace: survey
articles.title_zh: 26% in Japan see U.S. as biggest threat to world peace: survey
articles.content_orig:
A media association survey has found that the proportion of people in Japan who think the United States is the biggest threat to world peace came to 26.8%, the second highest after China, cited by 32.5%.
The rate for the United States rose 9.3 percentage points from the previous fiscal 2025 survey. The figure stood at 6.6% in fiscal 2024.
In the Japan Press Research Institute’s latest survey, released Saturday, participants were asked to pick one of the eight choices, including Russia and North Korea, as the country that they think poses the greatest threat to world peace.
China was up from second place, with its share rising 8.2 points.
Selected by 18.3%, Russia fell to third after ranking top in preceding surveys.
North Korea remained fourth, with 9.1%, while Iran, which has been in a military conflict with the United States, was chosen by 1.9%.
An official of the institute said that “the recognition that the United States poses a threat to the world is gradually expanding” due to the unpredictability of actions by U.S. President Donald Trump.
In the survey, a total of 82.5% of respondents said that Trump is having a negative impact on the world, including those who somewhat think so, up 3.1 points. The share of respondents who think Trump is having a positive impact came to 13.2%.
The survey also showed that 76.7% “very much” have or “somewhat” have a sense of crisis about a potential Taiwan contingency.
The survey was conducted between July 17 and Aug. 16, covering 5,000 people age 18 or over across Japan. Valid responses were received from 2,676.

articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
A federal judge in California has sentenced a former Syrian prison warden to 60 years for torturing inmates and lying to immigration officials to get into the United States.
A jury convicted Samir Ousman Alsheikh, 74, in March of conspiracy to commit torture, three counts of torture, one count of visa fraud and one count of attempted naturalization fraud, according to the U.S. attorney’s office in Los Angeles.
Alsheikh was involved in torturing political dissidents to deter opposition to the regime of then-Syrian President Bashar Assad, according to the Justice Department.
Government officials say Alsheikh is the highest-ranking former member of the Assad regime to be tried and convicted in person outside Syria.
The Justice Department had sought no fewer than 80 years in prison, while Alsheikh requested five years, citing his age and his chronic medical conditions.
In handing down the sentence on Thursday, U.S. District Judge Hernán Vera remarked on the “utter reprehensibility” of Alsheikh’s crime, Courthouse News Service reported .
“The conduct was heinous, unimaginably cruel and unspeakably violent and brutal,” the judge reportedly said.
Nina Marino, Alsheikh’s attorney, said her client plans to appeal the sentence.
In a statement, First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli said he hoped the sentence “gives some semblance of healing and closure to this defendant’s victims.”
“Criminals who inflict the type of savage brutality that this defendant did on his victims must never be granted refuge in our country,” Essayli said.
Samir Ousman Sheikh allegedly ordered inmates to a wing of a Syrian prison where they were then tortured with a device known as the ‘flying carpet.’
During Alsheikh’s trial, prosecutors presented evidence that Alsheikh ordered and participated in the torture of prisoners while he headed the Adra Prison, also known as Damascus Central Prison, from around 2005 to 2008.
Jurors heard testimony from three of Alsheikh’s victims who said they were packed into small, filthy, cold, wet cells that were infested with insects and other vermin. They described being tortured and seeing and hearing the torture of other prisoners.
The victims testified about being fastened to a device known as the “Flying Carpet,” which folded their bodies in half at the waist; about being manacled to the ceiling and suspended sometimes for days; and about being beaten while immobilized inside tires, according to the U.S. attorney’s office in L.A.
During the trial, prosecutors presented evidence that when detainees refused Alsheikh’s orders to harm political prisoners, he ordered them to be sent to an underground section of the prison known as Wing 13, where they were tortured.
Prosecutors also presented evidence that Alsheikh, who came to the country in 2020, lied to U.S. immigration authorities about his background to secure a green card and also on an application to naturalize as a U.S. citizen.
Alsheikh has been in custody since his arrest at Los Angeles International Airport in July 2024.
Khaled Abdul Malek, who testified about being detained and tortured under Alsheikh’s direction, praised the sentence in a statement .
“The land of freedom will never be a safe haven for slaughterers and those who committed crimes against humanity,” Malek said. “This trial is not the end, but the first step on the road toward accountability and justice for everyone whose hands have been stained with the blood of innocent people.”
